title: Hurting a monster with what you carry
target: How damage to a monster works in R.E.P.O. — the health behind it, the three sizes of impact, what objects do and what a death leaves behind.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A monster willing to stand still

steps.do: Think of a monster as carrying a health total rather than as indestructible.
steps.because: a monster carries a health total and a freeze time for dying (EnemyHealth, health, deathFreezeTime)

steps.do: Hit it hard on purpose, because impacts come in three sizes.
steps.because: impacts hurt it with separate damage for a light, a medium and a heavy one (impactHurt, impactLightDamage, impactMediumDamage, impactHeavyDamage)

steps.do: Throw things when a weapon is not the answer.
steps.because: being hurt by an object has its own switch, a multiplier and an option to stun (objectHurt, objectHurtMultiplier, objectHurtStun)

steps.do: Know that the stun is a choice the game makes, not a guarantee.
steps.because: the object-hurt options include whether it stuns (objectHurtStun)

steps.do: Expect some kills to pay out.
steps.because: a monster can be set to leave a valuable behind up to a maximum number (spawnValuable, spawnValuableMax)

steps.do: Read the feedback rather than only the health: being hurt, starting to die, dying and being hit by an object each signal.
steps.because: being hurt, starting to die, dying and being hurt by an object each raise an event (onHurt, onDeathStart, onDeath, onObjectHurt)

commonMistakes: Giving up on a monster that is taking damage but has not fallen yet.
Throwing things at a monster that cannot be stunned by objects.
Assuming every kill leaves something behind.
Missing the moment between starting to die and being dead.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
